extracted.intended_audience: researchers in scientometrics, peer-review studies, and authors of AI manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of full-text semantic, lexical, and psycholinguistic features of AI manuscripts to identify associations with peer-review acceptance and to predict review outcomes from word content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: "Accepted manuscripts scored lower than rejected manuscripts on two indicators of readability."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower scores on the two (unnamed in abstract) readability measures were associated with acceptance — i.e., accepted papers were less readable according to these indicators. Used as a metric to compare accepted vs rejected manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scientific and artificial intelligence jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: "Accepted manuscripts ... used more scientific and artificial intelligence jargon."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Density or frequency of domain-specific jargon (scientific / AI terminology) in the manuscript text; higher jargon use was associated with acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word frequency (lexical rarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Accepted manuscripts were written with words that are less frequent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average word frequency / rarity in the manuscript: accepted papers tended to use less frequent (more rare) words. This lexical measure differentiates accepted and rejected submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of acquisition of words
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Accepted manuscripts used words] that are acquired at an older age."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psycholinguistic measure: mean age-of-acquisition of words used in the manuscript. Higher age-of-acquisition values (words learned later) were associated with acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstractness of vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Accepted manuscripts used words] that are more abstract than rejected manuscripts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean concreteness/abstractness score of words: greater abstractness correlated with acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference overlap / citation similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: "The subset of accepted submissions were more likely to cite the same publications."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic metric measuring overlap or concentration of cited references across manuscripts; higher citation overlap among accepted manuscripts suggests common reference patterns associated with acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic similarity of word content across manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pairwise comparisons of the word content of the manuscripts (i.e. an indicator or semantic similarity) ... were more similar in the subset of accepted manuscripts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairwise semantic or lexical similarity measures (e.g., cosine similarity of content vectors) between manuscripts: accepted papers showed higher mutual similarity than rejected ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical word associations with acceptance (ML/neural vs logic/symbolic)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Words related to machine learning and neural networks [were] positively related with acceptance, whereas words related to logic, symbolic processing and knowledge-based systems [were] negatively related with acceptance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic- or keyword-level signals: presence/frequency of terms from subfields (e.g., machine_learning, neural_networks vs logic, symbolic_processing, knowledge-based_systems) had opposite associations with acceptance and can be used as predictive features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability of peer-review outcome from word content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Finally, we predicted the peer review outcome of manuscripts with their word content."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate predictive performance (classification) using textual features as input — indicates that word-content features provide signal sufficient to predict acceptance vs rejection. Can be interpreted as a measure of how informative textual dimensions are for peer-review outcome.
